html:
The Colonial Sugar Refining Company (CSR), an Australian firm, came to Fiji in 1880 and soon controlled its sugar industry, its main business for almost a century.

CSR built mills at Nausori, Lautoka and elsewhere and ran plantations worked by labourers of the Indian indenture. After indenture ended in 1920, the company leased small farms to Indo-Fijian growers, who cut cane on Fijian-owned land.

Strikes in 1921 and 1943 and disputes over prices marked its rule. In 1973 the government bought CSR's Fiji holdings, forming the Fiji Sugar Corporation. Sugar still matters in the west of Viti Levu, but tourism has passed it. See also sugarcane. Compare sugar in Hawaii.
sum: The Colonial Sugar Refining Company (CSR), an Australian firm, came to Fiji in 1880 and soon controlled its sugar industry, its main business for almost a century.
